security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline code spans, Java imports, and placeholder Azure URLs. No prompt injection, command execution, or exfiltration intent was found. The skill should add stronger safety guidance for purge, backup, and software-protected import examples.

remediation.issue: Local key backup example lacks storage controls.
remediation.suggestion: Describe secure storage, restricted file permissions, cleanup, and never committing backup blobs before showing backup and restore examples.

remediation.issue: Permanent purge is shown inside the normal delete flow.
remediation.suggestion: Move purge into a separate warning section and require explicit approval, recovery-window review, and break-glass procedures.

remediation.issue: Private key import example disables hardware protection.
remediation.suggestion: Mark software-protected import as test-only or exceptional, and show HSM-backed import guidance for production keys.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Key Backup Handling Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The backup section writes Key Vault backup bytes to key-backup.blob and reads them back without permission hardening or cleanup guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited example directly saves sensitive key backup data to a local file. The risk depends on user environment, but the missing storage controls are clear.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Purge Operation Without Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The delete section shows permanent key purge in the normal flow after deletion. Copying this pattern can cause irreversible key loss.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example includes purgeDeletedKey near delete and recover operations. It is legitimate SDK usage, but needs a stronger warning and approval context.

semantic_findings.title: Software-Protected Import Example for Private Key Material
semantic_findings.description: The import example builds a JsonWebKey with private RSA components and imports it with hardware protection disabled, without limiting it to test use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly handles private key components and sets hardware protection to false. This is valid for some cases, but unsafe as general production guidance.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Key Vault Keys in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need correct patterns for cloud key management and cryptographic operations. This skill gives focused Azure Key Vault Keys SDK guidance with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for the Azure Key Vault Keys Java package.
Demonstrates KeyClient and CryptographyClient creation with DefaultAzureCredential.
Covers RSA, EC, HSM-backed, and Managed HSM symmetric key examples.
Explains encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap operations.
Includes delete, recover, purge, backup, restore, and rotation examples.
Lists supported key types, encryption algorithms, and signature algorithms.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run Java code or provision Azure resources.
Users must provide their own vault, credentials, permissions, and tenant setup.
Examples use placeholders and need production review before deployment.
Destructive and sensitive operations require safeguards beyond the examples.

use_cases.title: Implement Key Management
use_cases.description: Build Java services that create, fetch, update, rotate, and list Azure Key Vault keys.

use_cases.title: Review Cryptography Flows
use_cases.description: Check encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap patterns before adding them to an application.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Key Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Compare HSM-backed keys, rotation policies, backup needs, and deletion controls for cloud workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Key Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for Azure Key Vault Keys in Java.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Key Vault Keys Java client with DefaultAzureCredential and a placeholder vault URL.

prompt_templates.title: Create Production Keys
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate key creation guidance for common key types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create RSA, EC, and HSM-backed keys with the Azure Key Vault Keys Java SDK. Include safe default choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design Crypto Operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Use the SDK for application cryptography workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Java workflow for encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap, and unwrap operations using Key Vault cryptography clients.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Key Lifecycle Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Java Key Vault key lifecycle plan for rotation, backup, restore, deletion, purge, HSM usage, and least privilege.

output_examples.input: I need a Java client setup for Azure Key Vault keys.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan with the Maven package, credential approach, vault URL placeholder, and client responsibilities.

output_examples.input: I need to decide between RSA, EC, and HSM keys.
output: A comparison of supported key types and typical use cases.
Guidance to prefer HSM-backed keys for sensitive production workloads.
Notes about key operations that should be enabled for each key.

output_examples.input: I want a key rotation and backup checklist.
output_examples.output: A review checklist covering rotation cadence, recovery expectations, backup storage controls, purge approvals, and access boundaries.

best_practices: Use least-privilege Azure roles and separate keys by application purpose.
Prefer HSM-backed keys for production secrets and regulated workloads.
Add explicit approval and recovery checks before delete, purge, backup, or restore actions.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder vault URLs, key names, or permissions into production unchanged.
Do not store key backup blobs in source control, shared folders, or unencrypted locations.
Do not use destructive purge examples without documented recovery and approval procedures.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides Java SDK guidance and examples for users who already manage their Azure environment.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include Azure authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use DefaultAzureCredential, but users must configure identities and permissions.

faq.question: Can it help with HSM-backed keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for hardware-protected RSA and EC keys, plus Managed HSM symmetric keys.

faq.question: Does it cover cryptographic operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers encryption, decryption, signing, verification, key wrapping, and key unwrapping.

faq.question: What should users review before production use?
faq.answer: Review identity permissions, HSM requirements, rotation policy, backup storage, deletion controls, and purge approvals.
